content:
mina: heads-up — bringing up stable-match-emb-v1 on staging. ran the quant pipeline (per-channel, 6-bit custom) and the smoke eval shows a recall@10 regression for short queries. dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/exp/SM-42 :eyes:

oliver: hmm ok. short queries as in < 8 tokens? can you paste the eval command + sample output?

mina: yeh short = <=8 tokens. ran: `python tools/eval_embeddings.py --model stable-match-emb-v1 --quant int6 --split webqa --k 10 --subset short`
output (summary):
```
baseline fp32 recall@10: 0.824
int6 (per-channel asym): 0.792
overall delta: -0.032
short-queries recall@10: baseline 0.812 -> int6 0.683
```

dana: that short drop is large. two quick things — are you L2-normalizing after quant? and are you using cosine vs dot? quant + no-postnorm often collapses directionality. also batchsize shouldn't matter here but curious if you used any post-calibration.

mina: used cosine and did L2 norm after quant. quant pipeline is asymmetric per-channel (scale + zero_point). no retrain calibration. sample code snippet for postnorm:
```
vec = quant_decode(qvec)
vec = vec / np.linalg.norm(vec, ord=2, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```
repro script lives in the experiment folder.

kai: can you share cluster metrics? maybe clusters flatten and silhouette drops.

mina: quick cluster stats: baseline silhouette=0.42, int6 silhouette=0.31. kmeans purity went from 0.78 -> 0.69 (k=1000). UMAP shows more overlap for topical anchors. linking heatmap: https://artifacts.internal/umap/SM-42.png

luis: try two experiments: 1) symmetric per-channel quant (no zp) and postquant L2 norm; 2) PQ fallback (OPQ+PQ 128) for short queries. PQ sometimes preserves local neighborhoods for small vectors. also run kmeans with init='kmeans++' and n_init=20.

mina: started job to re-run symmetric quant + L2 postnorm. launching eval for short + full splits.

deploy-bot: CI job started: quant-retrain-smoke-5511223344 (job id: jr-8420). logs: https://ci.internal/job/jr-8420

eval-bot: job jr-8420 finished — summary:
- symmetric per-channel + post-L2 recovered overall recall@10 to 0.815 (baseline 0.824)
- short-queries recall@10 improved to 0.79 (baseline 0.812)
- silhouette improved to 0.38
- latency +1.2% at p95 (same hardware)
full results: https://dash.internal/r/results/jr-8420

oliver: interesting — symmetric helped but short still down a bit. could be that the quantization error disproportionately affects short queries because they rely on sparser token signals? maybe try augmenting short-query holdout with a small distillation step?

mina: agreed. plan: 1) run OPQ+PQ fallback for short queries, 2) try tiny distill (100k pairs) and re-eval, 3) if stable, do a 5% canary on staging with monitoring on recall@k, cluster-purity, and latency.

dana: canary sounds good. add eval hooks to the route to compute recall snapshots every 5m. also alert if short-query recall@10 drops > 3% vs baseline.

mina: will create canary config tonight. snippet for rollout: `canary: {pct: 5, watch: [recall@10_short, p95_latency, cluster_purity]}`

luis: fyi try the PQ option with 128-subvectors and OPQ pre-rotate — had good short-query recovery on another model.

mina: thanks everyone. logging notes in the experiment doc and will post a follow-up with A/B results. :thumbsup:

oliver: thanks — ping when canary is up and I'll help watch the eval dashboards.

mina: will do.
